title: The Last Thorn Again
premise: Jude Thornbury has spent ten years hiding his swordspeech—the gift of commanding blades with spoken oaths—behind a smuggler's anonymity in the Thornfell mountains. When the crown's witch-hunters arrive and his sister Wren is seized as leverage, Jude learns she sold her own soul to the court beneath the mountain to buy his silence years ago. To free her, he must break his final oath, reveal himself to the hunt, and descend into the Undercourt before winter seals the passes. He wins her soul back at the cost of his gift—and discovers that an oath unspoken is finally, truly his own.
about_author: Gideon Ashgrove is the pen name of a former mountain guide who swears every story is true if you walk far enough to find it. They write fantasy about people bound by promises they never chose to make.

chapters.title: Salt on the Pass
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Smuggling iron through a snowbound pass, Jude quietly speaks a stuck gate open—his first use of the gift in years—and realizes a crown scout watched him do it. The beat: the fragile comfort of hiding, cracking.

chapters.title: The Proclamation at Millbrook
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In town he hears the edict: all swordspeakers to be taken alive for the war effort; harborers hanged. His old mentor's name is already on the list. The beat: dread hardening into resolve as Jude decides to run the mentor out over the pass.

chapters.title: What Wren Sold
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, now a court scribe, intercepts the hunt's orders and reveals in memory how she traded her soul to the Undercourt a decade ago to keep Jude's gift secret. The beat: guilt and fierce sisterly love colliding.

chapters.title: Hunters on the High Road
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Ambushed escorting his mentor, Jude speaks three oaths at once and shatters a hunting company—but the mentor dies anyway, and a survivor escapes with Jude's name. The beat: grief and the terrible relief of no longer pretending.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse Bargain
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A witch-tollkeeper offers passage beneath the mountain in exchange for one spoken oath, freely given—Jude binds himself to serve the road itself. The beat: the cost of love measured in chains he chooses.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Jude enters the Undercourt's bone-lit halls while Wren, above, sabotages the hunt to buy him time and is arrested for treason. The beat: two siblings racing each other toward sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. In the Undercourt, Jude finds Wren's soul kept as a singing jewel and bargains with the Pale Magistrate, who demands his gift entire—every oath he will ever speak. The beat: temptation, because surrender would make him safe forever.

chapters.title: Oathbreaker
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Instead of paying, Jude unsays his oldest oath—the one that bound him to silence—and the unleashed words tear the court's authority apart, freeing stolen souls including his mentor's. The beat: climax; loyalty to truth over duty to law.

chapters.title: Winter Seals the Passes
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Escaping upward through collapsing tunnels as the first true blizzard falls, Wren carries a voiceless, hollowed Jude while the hunt closes behind them. The beat: love against duty—she abandons her court career and name to save him.

chapters.title: The Last Thorn
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Spring-thaw epilogue: giftless but free, Jude plants his mentor's sword as a thornbush boundary stone and takes up ordinary smuggling routes with Wren beside him. The beat: quiet resolution—an inheritance remade as choice, not chain.
